title: AI-centered US stock bull market nears four-year anniversary
source_used: The Globe and Mail page carrying the Reuters article by Lewis Krauskopf (read in full)
key_facts: The S&P 500 is near record highs ahead of 12 Oct 2026, four years since its closing low for this cycle.
The current bull run has gained 117%, the sixth best since World War Two and the eighth longest.
S&P 500 earnings are expected to rise more than 35% this year, boosted by AI data-centre spending by the 'hyperscalers'.
Oxford Economics estimates about one-third of recent US economic growth stems from AI.
Nvidia's market value rose to US$5.8 trillion from US$286 billion on 12 Oct 2022; the top 10 S&P 500 companies' weight grew to about 40% from about 28% (J.P. Morgan Asset Management).
Risks: the Fed's recent pivot to rate hikes, a 10-year Treasury yield around 5.2% after reaching a 24-year high, midterm-election volatility and dependence on AI.
Anthony Saglimbene of Ameriprise said the 'easy money around AI has been made'.
quote_evidence: The U.S. bull market is going strong as it nears its four-year anniversary, driven by an AI spending engine that is propelling corporate profits and economic growth.
The weight of the top 10 companies in the S&P 500 has grown to about 40 per cent from about 28 per cent in October, 2022, according to J.P. Morgan Asset Management.
“The AI theme is the defining feature of this bull market,” said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise.
why_it_matters_hint: Gains and risks in the US stock market are increasingly tied to AI spending.
notes: The Reuters original (reuters.com URL in the pool, HTTP 401) was read through the Globe and Mail, which republishes it; credit goes to Reuters.
